title: Replication package: classification instability of the distance-decay choice in floating catchment accessibility
description: Code and derived results for a study quantifying how the choice of distance-decay (impedance) function changes the discrete classifications produced by two-step floating catchment area (2SFCA) accessibility measures, and bounding the defensible decay range by inverting decay from published person-trip origin-destination tables. Covers three Japanese metropolitan areas at 125 m resolution (566,885 populated cells, 145,078 medical facilities), six conventional decay specifications on pedestrian network distances, classification-stability diagnostics (pairwise disagreement, displacement, perturbation and copula null floors, designation turnover under relative and absolute rules), and a doubly constrained gravity inversion with bootstrap uncertainty.
